text:
Nick Seeler's week was defined by a moment on the bench. Early this week he and Matvei Michkov had a heated exchange that the Hockey News, NBC Sports Philadelphia and Broad Street Hockey all covered, with Danny Briere weighing in. Michkov's take, as Daily Faceoff headlined it: "When guys are emotional, this is good." Seeler, 33, has been the Flyers' blue-collar veteran for 370 games.

On the ice he is having a busier offensive season than usual: six assists in 22 games, after 10 points in 80 games last year. Our numbers say that pace runs ahead of what he does, since he has 0.72 expected goals (the quality of his own chances) and no goals on 16 shots, and Philadelphia has scored more than its chances suggest with him out there. The defensive side is the job: 54 blocked shots in about 19 minutes a night. At five on five the Flyers have taken 43% of the expected goals with him on, about the same as without him. He played 21.6 minutes in Saturday's win over Columbus, his most in the last ten games.
headline: Nick Seeler, the bench spat and the steady minutes
